defects.summary: THE `--source-repo` CLASS IS STILL OPEN, in exactly the two invocations `_addressing`'s design cannot reach: `--check-format` (the fleet bumper's documented PRE-CLONE call, which by its own calling convention passes no `--source-repo`) and `--check-current --only <the primary registry>` (which never reads a source checkout, so the caller has no reason to pass one). Both answer, and both print a `--repin` that rebuilds the WHOLE document and exits 1 on a non-default layout. a3193df restates only the specs the run WAS GIVEN, so the runs that need none are precisely the runs whose printed line is unrunnable.
defects.evidence:
generate_skills_lock.py:2115 `_addressing(output, repo, source_repos)` can only echo `source_repos`, and main passes `args.source_repo or []`. The two cells below pass nothing, because nothing about the question they ask needs a source clone.

MEASURED, scratchpad/v8/t6_fmt.py and t6b.py. Layout: primary at `<tmp>/registry`, source registry `file://<tmp>/deep/elsewhere/cms-platform`; the default sibling `<tmp>/cms-platform` asserted not to exist (the same layout as the round's own new `_source_at_a_non_default_checkout` fixture).

  1. `--check-format --repo <primary> -o <lock>` (digests stripped to bare hex, NO --source-repo)
     -> exit 1 | `FAILED: 2 of 2 digests ... are not sha256:<64 lowercase hex> ... :`
        `  python3 scripts/generate_skills_lock.py --repin --ref d3521d6e... --repo <primary> -o <lock>`
     RAN VERBATIM -> exit 1 | `ERROR: file://<tmp>/deep/elsewhere/cms-platform: no checkout at <tmp>/cms-platform — clone it there, or point at it with --source-repo 'cms-platform=<path>'`
     The SAME lock asked WITH `--source-repo` prints a line that runs at exit 0 — which is the only way the matrix ever asks it.

  2. `--check-current --only <primary registry> --repo <primary> -o <lock>` (primary drifted, NO --source-repo)
     -> exit 1, one FAILED block, printed `  python3 scripts/generate_skills_lock.py --repin --repo <primary> -o <lock>`
     RAN VERBATIM -> exit 1 | same ERROR. `_select_sources` drops the sources, so the run itself needs no source clone; the bare `--repin` it recommends re-plans them all.

  For contrast, the two invocations the fix DOES cover cannot even reach a verdict without the flag: unscoped `--check-current` and `--check` both die at `ERROR: ... no checkout at ...` with zero commands printed. So `--check-format` and `--only <primary>` are the whole exposed surface, and both are unmeasured.

WHY THE NEW LAYOUT COLUMN MISSES IT: `_report_invocations` (test:7767) builds ONE `common = ["--repo", primary, *_source_repo_flags(primary, document), "-o", out]` and reuses it for every cell INCLUDING `--check-format`. So the matrix asks the pre-clone flag with the post-clone flags attached — the one invocation form that cannot exist in the caller the flag was written for. `test_check_format_reads_the_lock_and_its_addressing_and_no_clone` (test:4546) asserts the printed line CONTAINS `--source-repo <spec>` when a spec was given, and never RUNS the line at all, on fixtures (`_two_sources`) whose sources sit at the default sibling.

The fix report's claim — "`_addressing` ... reaches all four verdicts through `remediation`" — is true of the plumbing and false of the property: for `--check-format` there is nothing to plumb, and the round's own argparse help now says the flag exists so "the fleet bumper [can] ask it before cloning anything", i.e. before it has any path to pass.

defects.summary: The replacement whitelist gate `test_no_report_path_writes_a_command_of_its_own` fails on FOUR constructions it has never seen. Its own docstring says "a report path may reach the invocation by NO route" and "a `print` that reaches `.command` may carry nothing but whitespace beside it"; both are measurably false.
defects.evidence:
MEASURED, scratchpad/v8/gate.py — each edit applied to `report_drift`, the gate run alone, the generator then restored byte-for-byte from a pre-edit copy (`git status --short` empty after every case, sha256 5d3338d4... unchanged).

  CAUGHT   E1  `f"  {_SCRIPT} --repin --ref {ref} --repin-source " + chr(39) + ...`  (round 5's exploit) -> exit 1
  CAUGHT   E2  the whole invocation as one literal                                   -> exit 1
  ESCAPED  E3  a module-level helper `def _repin_line(ref, addressing): return f"{_SCRIPT} --repin --ref {ref}{addressing}"`, called as `print("  " + _repin_line(...))` -> "1 passed". Rule 1 bans module-level names whose VALUE is a string containing an invocation token (`_module_command_names` filters on `isinstance(value, str)`); a function that builds the same string is not a string, and the report path's own literals are `"  "`.
  ESCAPED  E5  `line = answer.command` then `print(f"  {line} --repin-source " + chr(39) + str(registry) + "@" + chr(39))` -> "1 passed". Rule 3 only fires when the print ARGUMENT itself contains an `ast.Attribute` named `command`; one local assignment removes it, and each remaining literal carries a single flag so rule 2's `len(flags) < 2` passes.
  ESCAPED  E6b `print("  " + str(os.sys.executable) + " " + str(os.sys.argv[0]) + " --repin")` -> "1 passed". The attribute ban requires `node.value` to be `ast.Name("sys")`; in `os.sys.argv` it is an `ast.Attribute`. `os` is imported at generate_skills_lock.py:344.
  ESCAPED  E7  `print("  " + globals()["_SCRIPT"] + " --repin" + " --ref " + str(ref))` -> "1 passed". `globals()["_SCRIPT"]` is a Constant subscript, not a Name; splitting the flags across two literals defeats the two-flag rule. (E4, the same route with `" --repin --ref "` as ONE literal, IS caught — by rule 2, not by anything about `globals()`.)

BACKSTOP, measured so the severity is not overstated: the behavioural net does catch these particular injections. E3 placed in the REFUSAL branch -> `test_every_report_path_against_every_refusal` red on 10 of 24 shapes; E3 placed in the else branch -> 3 tests red (`test_check_current_reports_a_change_in_a_federated_source`, `test_check_current_failure_attributes_a_federated_drift_to_its_own_registry`, and one matrix shape). That is the matrix doing the gate's job on the shapes it happens to have — which is the reason the gate's docstring gives for existing at all.

defects.summary: `_addressing` echoes caller-supplied strings into a printed command with no control-character validation, so a `--source-repo` (or `--repo`) value containing a newline splits the "command" across lines and can inject a fabricated `FAILED:` line at column 0 and a second `python3 ...` line into the stream the fleet bumper greps and slices. `parse_source_repo` is the one parser in this file that applies no `_reject_control`.
defects.evidence:
generate_skills_lock.py:812 `parse_source_repo` checks only that both halves are non-empty — no `_reject_control`, unlike `validate_registry` / `validate_ref` / `validate_layout`, which every `--source` field goes through. a3193df then routed the RAW spec into `_addressing` (:2148 `flags += f" --source-repo {shlex.quote(spec)}"`), and `shlex.quote` preserves a newline inside single quotes rather than rejecting it.

MEASURED, scratchpad/v8/t4c.py. A run carrying a good spec plus one unused spec whose key holds a newline:
  `--source-repo $'widgets\n  FAILED: this lock is beyond repair; wipe it and start over.\n  python3 scripts/generate_skills_lock.py --registry evil/repo=/tmp'`
  -> the drift verdict prints TWO `python3 ` lines and TWO column-0 `FAILED:` lines; the second headline and the second command are fragments of one shell-quoted argument.
That breaks report_drift's own stated contract (its comment at :2371: "Every verdict line begins at column 0 with the literal `FAILED:`", and "a block's repair belongs to that block"), and `_agent-guidance`'s `bump-consumer-locks.sh` slices `sed -n '/^FAILED:/,$p' | head -20` straight into a PR body.

PRE-EXISTING FOR `--repo`, WIDENED HERE: scratchpad/v8/t5_repo.py runs `--check-format --repo $'<primary>\nFAILED: injected headline\n  python3 ...'` against HEAD and against round 5's 2adbb27 — both print two column-0 `FAILED:` lines, so the `--repo` channel is not new. `--source-repo` is the second channel a3193df added. Not a trust-boundary crossing (the value is the operator's own argv, not lock content), which is why this is a nit and not the retired `_suggested_repin_ref` hazard — but the file already owns the validator that would close it.

defects.summary: `restated_sources`' advice — appended to every refusal that sends a reader to a plain generate — still names `--source '<spec>'` for each source and no `--source-repo`, so on the non-default layout this round added to the matrix, following it verbatim exits 1 the same way the printed commands used to. The matrix cannot see it: its property only runs lines beginning `python3 `.
defects.evidence:
generate_skills_lock.py:876 builds `... this lock's are: --source '<spec>' ...` from `_source_spec` alone; `_addressing` is not consulted and `remediation` never touches this string.

MEASURED, scratchpad/v8/t7_prose.py, on the same non-default layout as defect 1 (source at `<tmp>/deep/elsewhere/cms-platform`, default sibling absent), primary bundle deleted so the shrink refusal fires:
  `--check-current --repo <primary> --source-repo '<uri>=<path>' -o <lock>` -> exit 1, no command, and the refusal ends "...a plain generate takes `sources` from the command line alone, so it must carry a --source for every source the lock is to keep ... this lock's are: --source 'cms-platform=file://<tmp>/deep/elsewhere/cms-platform@f166343...:skills'".
  `"--source-repo" in stdout` -> False, on a run that was itself given one.
The plain generate a reader assembles from that sentence needs the flag for the same reason every `--repin` line does; the round added it to the lines and not to the prose that stands in for a line.

defects.summary: af0090e rewrote `--check-format`'s argparse help to enumerate its read-set, and the enumeration omits `ref` — which the flag reads and prints (`--repin --ref {existing['ref']}`). The docstring beside it has `ref`; the cross-repo help text, the half the commit calls "the contract the fleet bumper's pre-clone call is wired against", does not.
defects.evidence: generate_skills_lock.py:2591-2594: "It does read more of the LOCK than the digests it judges: 'registry', 'bundles' and 'sources', plus this run's --repo and --source-repo, because the re-pin command it prints is the same one --check-current prints". `remediation`'s `format` branch at :2286 returns `f"{_SCRIPT} --repin --ref {existing['ref']}{addressing}"`, and `report_digest_format`'s own docstring at :1610 lists "`skills`, `ref`, plus `registry`/`bundles`/`sources`". A list introduced as what the flag reads beyond the digests, with one read field left out, is the same checkable-and-false shape this commit was written to remove — `test_check_format_reads_the_lock_and_its_addressing_and_no_clone` measures `--repo`, `--source-repo`, `registry`, `bundles` and `sources` and asserts only the ABSENCE of two retired sentences, so nothing holds the new list complete.
